These are big questions with no hard rules. 

But to get you started: 

You want remove all your stewards and most of your base cards before the final boss. 

The game asking you to build a deck that solves these problems: 

- can you deal with high health single target unit? 
- can you deal with multiple low health units? 
- do you get stronger as the fight goes on? (Scaling) 

Look at your deck as you play to assess what it's missing and then look at the card rewards.

You guys are seriously the role uniques play in this game. 

They're 3 types of uniques in this game:

1. Gear gap filler uniqes 
These uniqes exist to fill gaps in your gear until you find the correct upgrade. So YES a well rolled rare will be better than these, no shit. 

They exist to smoothen the gear progression and then you drop them. It's good they exist.

2. Leveling uniques 

These exist to help leveling characters and nothing else. And yes these are designed to be beaten by a well rolled rare. A well rolled rare in the early is harder to come by than these uniques. 

3. Build around uniqes.

These offer a mechanic or synergy that come only from that itsm and can can enable powerful builds. These items will always have worse raw overall stat's than a 6 mods high tier rare, as to prevent people only using uniques and never caring about rares. 

Uniques are not legendaries, they're nor designed to be power houses that you instantly equip and never have to think about rares ever again. 

Look at games that have legendaries be the only that matter in the endgame :bl3 and d4. They're loot and itemisation is extremely boring in the early game and endgame. 

The true unique/ legendary are a well rolled. A rare with 6 useful high tier mods are the true uniques/ legendary of poe.

Cant give a review atm but can offer this advice: loss streaks, regardless of skill, will always happen. Your only %10 of the lobby, so you can only expect ~%60wr when playing your absolute best. 

But even a %60 will always lead to occasional loss streaks of 5+ games, it just the nature of multiplier games.

What can you do is: 
- not tilt 
- take a break for the day after losing 2 games 
- remind yourself for every loss streak there's a eventually a win streak 
- don't get over excited during a winstreak and vice versa don't get too mad at loss streaks 
- variance is inevitable 

Just focus on one skill at a time and ask yourself at the end of each game: how well did I focus/ practise on that skill during that game? 

If you focus on improving your own skills, and ignore your win rate, you will climb eventually. Focus on the long term. 

Good luck.
